title: Choose PPM Finance's visual direction
question: Pick the visual world that should shape the redesigned screening and monitoring workspace. Each keeps the existing product behavior and labels synthetic history as demo data.

options.label: Character Atlas
options.thesis: A friendly, finite roster makes each company easy to scan and revisit.
options.viewport: PPM Finance opens on the Screen workspace: standard navigation, a ticker search, one selected-company profile, clear criterion states, and a small, explicitly synthetic demo growth chart. A tracked-company roster uses whole, responsive cells. The signature move is one saturated ribbon that marks the selected ticker and follows its state across the roster and review flow.
options.risk: The catalog language can feel playful rather than financially serious; keep company data and state labels more prominent than decorative treatment.

options.label: Shareholder Report
options.thesis: A clear editorial hierarchy turns screening evidence into a readable research brief.
options.viewport: The standard app navigation frames a focused company screen. A strong ticker heading leads into four criterion results, each paired with its value and source state; an annotated multi-year demo chart sits beside the criteria when synthetic history is shown. The signature move is a precise chart annotation that connects a change point to the criterion it may affect.
options.risk: Annual-report styling is familiar; it must stay product-like and interactive rather than becoming a static editorial page.

options.label: Acetate Reference Manual
options.lineage: tabbed reference manuals with clear overlays
options.thesis: Each screening rule reads like a concise, navigable reference entry.
options.viewport: Familiar app navigation anchors the Screen, Tracking, and Approval jobs. The main result pairs a readable company summary with four directly comparable rules; an expandable layer explains thresholds and data sources. A multi-year demo chart uses one clear year axis. The signature move is a hinged, two-step reveal for threshold and source details, never an overlay that obscures the result.
options.case: Wins on both audience identification and product clarity: researchers value explainable rules, and the indexed reference pattern teaches each threshold without changing familiar controls.
options.risk: Too many reveal layers could slow scanning; keep primary evidence visible and explanations optional.

options.label: Time-Series Timetable
options.thesis: A disciplined year-by-year rhythm makes comparisons and changes legible.
options.viewport: Standard navigation keeps the product recognizable. A company header leads into a multi-year demo growth chart, followed by a chronological evidence table and the current pass/fail/unknown screen. The signature move is a shared year cursor: selecting a year highlights the matching chart point and table column.
options.case: Wins on both axes: the timeline directly answers the request to compare growth across years, while shared year selection clarifies how chart and screening evidence relate.
options.risk: A one-size, highly compressed data rhythm may reduce readability; use clear type hierarchy and switch to stacked rows on narrow screens.

options.label: Research Journey
options.lineage: jet-age ticket wallets and sequential coupons
options.thesis: Screen, save, compare, and review feel like clear steps in one research journey.
options.viewport: Standard navigation stays fixed while the company workflow is expressed as four familiar steps: Screen, Results, Track, and Review. The first view prioritizes the selected ticker and its criteria, with the current step and next action always visible. The signature move is a persistent progress strip that records completed and pending research steps without implying a trade.
options.case: Competitive: the journey makes the workflow unusually easy to learn, but its sequential metaphor is less natural for researchers who move repeatedly between companies and criteria.
options.risk: A step-by-step presentation could imply a one-way process; all areas must remain directly reachable.

options.label: Exposure Record
options.lineage: darkroom exposure records and tonal zone sheets
options.thesis: Layered marks make the magnitude and confidence of evidence visible.
options.viewport: A company result sits over a tonal scale; criterion values, missing inputs, and status changes are distinguished through labeled marks and hatching. The signature move is an annotated change overlay that never treats missing data as a failure.
options.case: Declined: it offers an inventive way to encode confidence but asks investors to learn a specialized visual vocabulary before screening a company.
options.kept: Keep its commitment to showing evidence changes explicitly and never relying on color alone.
options.risk: Hatching and overlapping sheets could obscure values and overcomplicate a first-time screen.

options.label: Constructed Data Grid
options.lineage: modernist typographic specimens and visible construction grids
options.thesis: A visible measurement grid makes quantitative evidence feel deliberate and comparable.
options.viewport: A familiar finance workspace uses aligned cells for criteria, values, and a labeled synthetic growth chart. One accent plane marks the active year and its related evidence. The signature move is a shared construction grid that aligns chart ticks and table columns.
options.case: Declined: the grid aids quantitative comparison but contributes less to the learnability and evidence explanation the brief prioritizes.
options.kept: Keep a visible, consistent alignment between chart scales and comparison tables.
options.risk: A permanently visible grid can add noise and make the interface feel like a design specimen.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: A polished, familiar finance dashboard with no deliberate outside-world reference.
canonCard.viewport: A conventional left navigation rail and top ticker search lead to a company summary, criterion cards, a chart, tracked companies, and review actions. The visual signature is restrained use of standard finance status colors.
canonCard.risk: Familiar and easy to read, but less distinctive than a fully committed visual system.
